`lib` adds DOM because this really is browser code — IndexedDB, and later the
content scripts and extension pages, are typed only there. `types` stays empty
(inherited from tsconfig.base.json) on purpose: a Chrome MV3 service worker has no
Node runtime, so a `process.env` or `Buffer` reference in the extension is a bug that
would ship, and it must fail here rather than at load time in a user's browser.
This is deliberately not merged into gate 1. Gate 1 proves capsule-schema and
capsule-core compile with neither Node nor DOM available; folding the app in would
mean granting DOM to that program and losing the only mechanical check that the
DOM rather than WebWorker: the extension has both page and worker surfaces, and the
APIs used across the boundary between them (IndexedDB, structured clone) are declared
in lib.dom. A worker-only lib would fail to type the popup and options pages.
